top news.title: SpaceX raises $75B in the biggest-ever IPO, pricing 555.6M shares at $135 each, giving it a market value of $1.77T

tweets.author: @danprimack
tweets.text: Gonna read a lot about VC “returns” from the SpaceX IPO. Reminder that no VC is selling shares into the IPO, and can't sell for a while. So these are still paper gains, not actual cash for distribution-starved LPs in their funds.

tweets.author: @eastdakota
tweets.text: Anyone remember what $NET's IPO “pop” was? I like @matt_levine calling it “perfect” — to the penny. You have a lot more control of what happens when you price an IPO than it may seem. If @elonmusk turns out to have called it even close to perfect two weeks in advance... 🤯 [image]

tweets.author: @andrewcurran_
tweets.text: SpaceX has excluded investors from China and Hong Kong from participating in its IPO, according to the NYT. The article also reports that OpenAI is likely to impose the same restrictions when it goes public. Given past statements from Anthropic, they may also do the same. [image]

top news.title: Sources: OpenAI is considering drastically lowering the prices it charges users for tokens in anticipation of similar cuts the startup expects Anthropic to make

tweets.author: @mweinbach
tweets.text: If OpenAI does drop token pricing, this is likely because they've heard from customers they can't adopt AI at volume at the current pricing. Margin is high now for served tokens. They could cut prices by like 60% and still be profitable imo

tweets.author: @edzitron
tweets.text: Both OpenAI and Anthropic are considering price cuts. Neither of these companies but ESPECIALLY OpenAI can under any circumstances afford this pay cut. This is fundamentally insane. A sign of desperation that will erode revenue while costs stay linear.  [image]

top news.title: Anthropic backtracks on its decision to quietly limit Fable 5's ability to develop LLMs, saying “requests will visibly fall back to Opus 4.8”, after backlash

tweets.author: @claudedevs
tweets.text: We're rolling out changes to make Fable 5's safeguards for frontier LLM development visible.  Starting this week, flagged requests will visibly fall back to Opus 4.8—the same as our safeguards for cyber and bio.  You will see this every time it happens.  On the API, any flagged requests will return a reason for their refusal (coming to server-side fallback in the next few days).

tweets.author: @zeffmax
tweets.text: “We're changing Fable 5's safeguards for frontier LLM development to make them visible,” Anthropic tells WIRED.  “We made the wrong tradeoff and we apologize for not getting the balance right.”

tweets.author: @deanwball
tweets.text: This resolves the central concern I had with the Fable release, which was the silent degradation.  I am glad to see Anthropic make the right call here.  That said, I suspect the residual broken trust and resentment this has created will linger and will have a blast radius wider than Anthropic (the next time I advocate for any policy justified by AI risk concerns, I almost guarantee you this incident will be used in rebuttal).
